page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3c.14xlarge is a dedicated big data instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. The virtual machine provisions 56 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 224.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM allocated per vCPU. Virtualization is handled via KVM, and the instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

A defining hardware feature of the ecs.d3c.14xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 54975 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. This local disk configuration provides dense raw storage directly attached to the host, bypassing network-attached storage latency for data access. Network connectivity is supported by a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth, which accommodates high-throughput node-to-node communication within distributed environments. The server does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Regarding hardware efficiency, coupling high-capacity mechanical drives with a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio delivers economical per-terabyte storage density relative to solid-state alternatives. However, the presence of spinning HDDs introduces standard mechanical constraints: random input and output operations per second are limited compared to NVMe media, focusing performance characteristics toward sequential throughput and capacity-oriented tasks.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3c.14xlarge is tailored for large-scale distributed data architectures and analytics frameworks. Typical deployments include Apache Hadoop clusters, Apache Spark workloads, distributed log processing systems like Apache Kafka, and batch extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines requiring high local storage density.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3c.14xlarge is a big data instance designed for distributed storage and analytics workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8369B processors clocked at 2.9 GHz, it features 56 dedicated vCPUs and 224.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 54975 GB of local HDD storage, offering substantial capacity for data-intensive processing without requiring remote block storage attachments. Network connectivity provides a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth to support heavy node-to-node data transfers across compute clusters. Operating under KVM virtualization without GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance balances compute cores with high-density local mechanical disks. This profile makes ecs.d3c.14xlarge suited for big data architectures, distributed file systems, Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark, and batch extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines requiring high sequential storage capacity.
